PerfectoidQuotients.summary: Nothing prismatic exists in the pinned baseline: `prism`, `δ-ring`, `p-derivation`, `quasisyntomic`, `semiperfectoid`, `perfectoidization` and `Nygaard` all have zero hits in Mathlib's 246k and Tau Ceti's 71k declarations, and neither library even defines a perfectoid ring. What the libraries do supply is the integral prefix of Q0: Mathlib's Witt vectors (Frobenius, Verschiebung, Teichmüller, ghost components, truncation) together with `Perfection`/`PreTilt`, the multiplicative untilt, `WittVector.fontaineTheta : 𝕎 R♭ →+* R` for any p-adically complete R and its surjectivity when Frobenius is surjective on R/p — so A_inf = W(R♭) and θ are available, in greater generality than BS22 assumes, all sorry-free. Also available as generic input: ordinary adic completion, flatness and faithfully flat descent for modules, regular sequences, divided power structures and the two-term cotangent complex. Genuinely missing is everything the roadmap actually plans: the principal generator of ker θ, derived p-adic completion, animated/simplicial commutative rings, δ-rings and prisms, prismatic cohomology and the Hodge–Tate comparison, universal prisms and perfectoidization, André's flatness lemma and the closed-quotient theorem 7.4/5.8.

targets.target: Integral perfectoid ring in the BS22 sense (p-adically complete, Frobenius surjective on R/p, kernel of θ principal)
targets.note: Neither library defines a perfectoid ring: `grep -rni perfectoid` over both trees returns only Mathlib/RingTheory/Perfection.lean and the three files of Mathlib/RingTheory/Perfectoid/, and none of them introduces a predicate. Mathlib works instead with the separate hypotheses `[IsAdicComplete (span {(p:R)}) R]` and `Function.Surjective (frobenius (ModP R p) p)`, and its own TODO in BDeRham.lean records that `ker θ` principal for integral perfectoid rings is not yet proved.

targets.target: Comparison of integral perfectoid rings with perfectoid Tate rings, and the integral subrings R°, R⁺
targets.note: Tau Ceti has Tate rings and the power-bounded subring A° (with A°° an ideal of it), so the integral-subring vocabulary exists, but there is no perfectoid Tate ring and hence no comparison; `IsUniform`/`IsStablyUniform` do not exist in either tree.

targets.target: A_inf = W(R♭) with θ : A_inf → R and its explicit description
targets.note: Mathlib builds R♭ = `PreTilt R p` = Perfection(R/p), the multiplicative untilt (sharp) map and `fontaineTheta : 𝕎 R♭ →+* R` for any p-adically complete R, with surjectivity under Frobenius surjectivity on R/p — more general than BS22's hypothesis. The standard base is there too: ℂ_[p] is built as the p-adic completion of an algebraic closure of ℚ_[p], proved nonarchimedean and algebraically closed, with ring of integers `PadicComplexInt` and a `Valuation.Integers` witness, all sorry-free. Missing: the principal non-zero-divisor generator of ker θ, the (p,[ϖ])-adic topology on A_inf, the residue map to W(k), and even an `IsAdicComplete (span {p}) 𝓞_ℂ_[p]` instance, so θ is not yet instantiated at O_C.

targets.target: Ordinary, derived p-adic and pseudouniformizer-adic completions kept separate
targets.note: Ordinary I-adic completion (`AdicCompletion`, `IsAdicComplete`) and the topological completion of a Huber ring exist; derived (p-complete) completion of a module or ring does not — `IsDerivedComplete`/`derivedCompletion` have no hits in either tree.

targets.note: `semiperfect` matches only `TauCeti.IsSemiperfectRing` (a Jacobson-radical notion in TauCeti/RingTheory/Jacobson/Semiperfect.lean, unrelated), and `semiperfectoid` has zero hits in both trees.

targets.note: `delta-ring`, `δ-ring` and `p-derivation` have zero hits in both trees. Mathlib has Witt-vector Frobenius and the Teichmüller lift, which is the comparison material the layer asks for, but no δ-structure.

targets.note: `prism` has zero hits as a substring anywhere in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (216 008 + 70 802 declarations), so none of these notions exists.

targets.note: Only the perfection functor itself (`Perfection`, `PerfectionMap`, `PreTilt`) is available; there is no prism side of the correspondence.

targets.target: Existing Witt-vector constructions, with every Frobenius lift compared to them
targets.note: The Witt-vector side is fully built: Mathlib/RingTheory/WittVector/ has 20 sorry-free files covering Frobenius, Verschiebung, Teichmüller, ghost components, truncated Witt vectors, the DVR structure over a perfect field and F-isocrystals, so nothing there needs constructing. Only the comparison half of the target is missing, and it is missing because there are no δ-structures to compare with.

targets.note: Idempotents and retracts exist generically; none of these prismatic statements does.

PerfectoidSpaces.summary: Tau Ceti already contains a substantial non-perfectoid foundation for this roadmap: Huber and Tate rings with pairs of definition, pseudouniformizers, the power-bounded subring A° and A°°, rings of definition, completion, the topological localization A⟨T/s⟩ with its universal property and presentation independence, strong noetherianness, the valuation spectrum and continuous valuations, Spa(A,A⁺) as a spectral space, rational subsets with their basis/refinement/perturbation calculus, the homeomorphism Spa(A⟨T/s⟩) ≅ R(T/s), Wedhorn 8.32's faithful flatness of a rational cover, residue-field valuations, and the reduction of sheafhood to rational covers — all sorry-free. Mathlib adds the two pieces of P0 and P1 the roadmap treats as work: the Serre quotient of an abelian category by a Serre class is proved abelian (`SerreClassLocalization.abelian`), and Fontaine's θ : 𝕎 R♭ →+* R with its surjectivity is proved for every p-adically complete ring, together with `Perfection`/`PreTilt`, the multiplicative untilt and B_dR. Everything perfectoid is missing: no library defines a perfectoid ring, there is no almost mathematics, no tilting equivalence or almost purity, no adic spaces (only affinoid spectra), no sheaf theorem or Čech/sheaf-cohomology comparison, no completed tensor products or fibre products, no tilde-limits, no finite group quotients, and no v-sheaves or pro-étale calculus. Mathlib's own TODO records that ker θ principal is unproved, which is one of P1's stated targets.

targets.target: Abstract base (V, 𝔪) with an idempotent ideal satisfying the flatness/tensor hypotheses of almost ring theory
targets.note: `almost math`, `almostification` and `almost zero` have zero hits in both trees. Ideals form a commutative semiring so `IsIdempotentElem (𝔪 : Ideal V)` is expressible, but the almost-base package (𝔪 = 𝔪², 𝔪 ⊗_V 𝔪 flat) is not defined anywhere.

targets.target: Almost-zero modules as a Serre subcategory
targets.note: Mathlib's `ObjectProperty.IsSerreClass` is exactly the closure-under-subobjects/quotients/extensions condition such a class must satisfy, so only the instance (`𝔪 M = 0`) is missing; the class itself has no definition in either tree.

targets.target: The Serre quotient of the module category
targets.note: Fully present and more general: for any Serre class `P` in an abelian category `C` and any localization functor at `P.isoModSerre`, `SerreClassLocalization.abelian` proves the target abelian, with both calculi of fractions, mono/epi criteria and the exactness criterion for functors out of it. The file has no `sorry` (the 'future work' note in SerreClass/Basic.lean is stale). Applying it to almost-zero modules needs only the class itself.

targets.target: Almostification and its adjoints
targets.note: Mathlib relates a Serre localization to Bousfield localization when a left adjoint exists, but the module-theoretic almostification M ↦ 𝔪 ⊗ M and M ↦ alHom(𝔪, M) and the adjunctions are not constructed.

targets.target: Tensor and Hom of almost modules
targets.note: No almost modules, hence no monoidal or internal-Hom structure on them.

targets.target: Almost-flat and almost-finite-projective modules
targets.note: Only ordinary flatness/projectivity; the 'almost' variants have no hits.

targets.target: Almost algebras and almost finite étale algebras
targets.note: Mathlib has the category of finite étale algebras (`CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale`) and `Algebra.Etale`; the almost versions do not exist.

targets.target: Instantiation by the ideal of positive fractional powers of a pseudouniformizer: idempotence, flatness, independence of the choice, comparison of the almost categories from R⁺ and R°
targets.note: Tau Ceti has pseudouniformizers and the power-bounded subring A° with A°° an ideal, but no fractional powers ϖ^{1/p^n} (which need a perfectoid ring) and no almost category.

targets.target: Descent for almost modules and almost algebras along faithfully flat maps
targets.note: Ordinary faithfully flat descent of modules (extension of scalars comonadic) and abstract descent data on a site exist in Mathlib; there is no almost version.

targets.target: Passage between compatible integral reductions, completion and inversion of a pseudouniformizer, with torsion-freeness, completeness and uniform bounds
targets.note: Tau Ceti has the topological completion of a Huber ring, power-boundedness transfer across it, and localization at a pseudouniformizer inside the Huber-localization API; the uniform bounds stated for almost-module limit arguments are not formulated.

targets.target: The 'almost exact ⇒ exact after inversion' theorem, with the derived inverse-limit term shown to vanish
targets.note: No almost exactness; and `lim^1`/`Rlim` for inverse systems of modules has no hits in either tree, so the derived-limit term could not be named.

targets.target: Čech and sheaf-cohomology formulations of almost cohomology
targets.note: Mathlib defines sheaf cohomology `Sheaf.H F n` as Ext from the constant sheaf, and a Čech complex functor for a family of objects, but proves no comparison between the two (Cech.lean contains only the construction), which is the comparison this layer and P2 need.

duplicates.note: P3 consumes this stage's integral almost-algebra lifting and almost-finite-étale notions for almost purity; P0 explicitly excludes the purity theorem itself.
D6's tilting/diamond comparison reuses the same almost-module and tilting apparatus at the level of analytic adic spaces.

targets.target: Perfectoid Tate ring (ECD 3.1): complete uniform Tate ring with ϖ such that ϖ^p | p in R° and Frobenius R°/ϖ → R°/ϖ^p an isomorphism
targets.note: Tau Ceti supplies `IsTateRing`, `IsPseudoUniformizer` and `A°`, and `CompleteSpace`/`T0Space` carry completeness and separatedness; but there is no uniformity predicate for a Huber ring in the Hansen–Kedlaya sense (A° bounded): `IsStablyUniform` has zero hits, and the `IsUniform*` names in Mathlib are uniform-space notions. The condition is one line away rather than a theory to build: `Huber.IsBounded S` (∀ U ∈ 𝓝 0, ∃ V ∈ 𝓝 0, V * S ⊆ U) applied to `powerBoundedSubring` states it. There is also no perfectoid condition anywhere in either library.

targets.target: Equivalent Frobenius-surjectivity criterion with the pseudouniformizer condition retained
targets.note: Depends on the absent definition.

targets.target: Characteristic-p characterization as perfect complete Tate rings
targets.note: Both ingredients exist separately (`PerfectRing R p`, `IsTateRing`, and K⸨X⸩ as a worked Tate example) but the equivalence is not stated.

targets.target: Perfectoid-field characterization, and that ℚ_p is not perfectoid
targets.note: Tau Ceti proves ℚ_p is a Tate ring with pseudouniformizer p and that ℤ_p is Huber but not Tate; the perfectoid-field notion and the non-example statement are absent.

targets.target: The multiplicative inverse limit R♭ with its limiting addition, topology, sharp map and functoriality
targets.note: Mathlib's `PreTilt O p = Perfection(O/p)` is the p-adic tilt with its ring structure, Frobenius bijectivity, coefficients, and (for a valued field with ring of integers) a valuation and domain property; `PreTilt.untilt` is the multiplicative sharp map to O and is a `MonoidHom`, not asserted additive, exactly as the layer requires. Missing: the ϖ-adic Tate tilt (lim R°/ϖ) and its identification with this p-adic one, the topology on R♭ and completeness/uniformity of R♭.

targets.target: Completeness, uniformity, characteristic p, and descriptions of the integral subrings of R♭
targets.note: Characteristic p and (for a valued field) the domain property and valuation are proved; completeness, uniformity and the integral-subring descriptions are not, because R♭ carries no topology in Mathlib.

targets.target: Fontaine's θ : W(R♭) → R and its surjectivity
targets.note: Present and more general than the layer asks: `fontaineTheta : 𝕎 R♭ →+* R` is built for every p-adically complete commutative ring R, θ([x]) = x^♯ is proved, and `surjective_fontaineTheta` gives surjectivity under exactly the hypothesis that Frobenius is surjective on R/p — which an integral perfectoid ring satisfies. Both files are sorry-free. The caveat is that this θ is stated on the p-adic tilt and does not carry the Tate topology.

targets.target: The principal non-zero-divisor description of ker θ
targets.note: Not proved: Mathlib's own TODO in BDeRham.lean lists 'Show that ker θ is principal when the base ring is integral perfectoid' as future work, and `BDeRham` is defined by inverting the set of generators of ker θ precisely to avoid needing it.

targets.target: Classification of marked untilts by primitive degree-one ideals, with the converse construction, its topology and plus ring (ECD 3.14–3.17)
targets.note: `primitive degree` and `marked untilt` have zero hits; only the single-element untilt map exists.

targets.target: Equivalence of perfectoid algebras over R and over R♭, with unit, counit and naturality
targets.note: The tilting equivalence is absent from both libraries.

targets.target: Tests: completed 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞})), cyclotomic and compatible-root mixed-characteristic fields, perfected Tate balls/tori, a non-field perfectoid Tate ring
targets.note: The un-perfected models exist — K⸨X⸩ as a Tate ring, the closed polydisc over a Huber pair, cyclotomic extensions, ℚ_p, and ℂ_[p] as the complete algebraically closed p-adic field with its ring of integers — but no perfection of any of them is constructed, and none is shown perfectoid.

duplicates.note: Q0's integral prefix builds the integral perfectoid/A_inf/θ side and compares it with 'Tate perfectoid rings', i.e. with this layer.
F4 restates the marked-untilt classification through the primitive kernel of θ as a Cartier divisor on Y_F.
RF2 ('Untilts, divisors and local de Rham rings') states the same untilt/divisor dictionary in the relative setting.
AI.0 fixes the same θ and its kernel generator for O_C and normalizes μ, ξ and tilde-ξ.
The Tau Ceti library roadmap's Layer 6 packages the perfectoid-field input, W(𝒪_F) and A_inf that this layer's integral side needs.

targets.target: Tilting homeomorphism of valuation spectra and its rational-subset correspondence, beyond rank one
targets.note: Tau Ceti has Spa(A,A⁺) as a spectral space with rational subsets, a basis of quasi-compact opens, perturbation and refinement results, and functorial pullback; the tilting homeomorphism needs the (absent) tilt of a perfectoid Tate ring.

targets.target: Perfectoid rational localizations and the identification of their tilts
targets.note: The rational localization A⟨T/s⟩ exists in Tau Ceti with its topological universal property, presentation independence, restriction maps, and the homeomorphism Spa(A_U, A_U⁺) ≅ R(T/s); what is missing is that it is perfectoid when A is, and the identification of its tilt.

targets.target: Sheaf theorem and all-degree almost acyclicity on affinoids and their integral structure sheaves (ECD 3.18, 3.24)
targets.note: Tau Ceti has the presentation-indexed structure presheaf (explicitly not yet identified with 𝒪_X), the reduction of sheafhood to rational covers, and Wedhorn 8.32's faithful flatness of a rational cover for a strongly noetherian Tate ring — real progress toward the classical sheaf theorem, but neither `IsSheafyPair` nor any acyclicity statement exists, and almost acyclicity needs P0.

targets.target: Acyclic basis comparison passing from rational Čech exactness to sheaf cohomology
targets.note: The basis-cover criterion for sheafhood is proved in Tau Ceti and Mathlib has both a Čech complex functor and sheaf cohomology as Ext, but no theorem comparing Čech and sheaf cohomology (even for an acyclic basis) exists in either tree.

targets.target: Perfectoid spaces as the full subcategory of adic spaces locally modelled on perfectoid Huber pairs
targets.note: There is no category of adic spaces in either library: `AdicSpace`, `PreAdicSpace` and Wedhorn's 𝒱/𝒱^pre have no hits, and Tau Ceti stops at the affinoid adic spectrum.

targets.target: Gluing of tilting and the slice-category equivalence ECD 3.20
targets.note: Needs tilting and adic spaces, both absent.

targets.target: Fibre products of perfectoid spaces, their affine formulas with completed/uniform integral algebra, perfectoidness, universal property, and compatibility with tilting
targets.note: `completed tensor` has zero hits in both trees, so even the affine input is missing.

targets.target: Products in Perf, with Spec 𝔽_p not treated as a perfectoid Tate space
targets.note: No category Perf.

targets.target: Completed residue fields and their plus rings
targets.note: Tau Ceti constructs κ(v) = (supp v).ResidueField with the valuation of v extended to it (Wedhorn §2.4); the completion of κ(v) and its valuation subring are not constructed.

duplicates.note: The Tau Ceti library roadmap owns rational localisation, the structure presheaf 𝒪_X and 𝒪_X⁺, and pre-adic spaces; that is the non-perfectoid half of this layer and is partly built already.
Layer 4 owns the classical sheaf theorem and all-degree Čech exactness for strongly noetherian and stably uniform Tate rings, which P2 refines to the perfectoid/almost case.
Layer 5 owns adic spaces, open/closed immersions and gluing, the carrier on which P2 defines perfectoid spaces.
A0 owns the completed tensor products and the fibre products this layer uses for products of perfectoid spaces.
D6 glues tilting for analytic adic spaces into the diamond comparison, overlapping the slice-equivalence statement.

targets.target: ECD 6.1(a): a finite étale algebra over a perfectoid Tate ring is perfectoid
targets.note: Mathlib has finite étale algebras as a category with base change, but no perfectoid rings, so the statement cannot be made.

targets.target: ECD 6.1(b): tilting is an equivalence on finite étale algebras
targets.note: No tilting functor.

targets.target: ECD 6.1(c): integral closures of finite étale algebras are almost finite étale
targets.note: Ordinary integral closure exists; 'almost finite étale' requires P0's almost algebra, which is absent.

targets.target: The integral almost-algebra lifting theorem

Also available as generic input: `WittVector.Isocrystal` (a φ-semilinear module over Frac W(k) with the one-dimensional Dieudonné–Manin classification), integral Galois lattices, and abstract p-adic measures. Genuinely missing is the whole (φ,Γ)-module engine and every theorem PG.0–PG.7 states about it.

PrismaticCohomology.summary: This roadmap is untouched by the baseline. `prism`, `δ-ring`, `p-derivation`, `Nygaard`, `quasisyntomic`, `syntomic`, `Cartier-Witt`, `F-crystal`, `Breuil`, `decalage`/`Lη`, `log structure`, `prelog`, `fs monoid`, `Spf`, `q-analog` and `de Rham-Witt` all have zero hits in Mathlib's 246k and Tau Ceti's 71k declarations, and neither library has algebraic de Rham cohomology, crystalline cohomology, étale cohomology, an étale site, algebraic stacks, formal schemes, derived completion, animated rings or derived exterior powers. What is available is the input layer PR.0 asks to be matched against: Mathlib's Witt vectors (Frobenius, Verschiebung, Teichmüller, ghost components, truncation, the DVR structure over a perfect field, F-isocrystals with the one-dimensional Dieudonné–Manin classification), `Perfection`/`PreTilt` with `fontaineTheta` and its surjectivity, divided power structures with sub-PD-ideals and the divided power algebra (but no PD envelope), the two-term cotangent complex with H^1 and base change, Kähler differentials, adic completion, flatness/faithful flatness and regular sequences, Grothendieck topologies, sheaves, sheaf cohomology as Ext, a Čech complex functor, the derived category and abstract descent data, and the rings W(k), W(k)[[u]], ℤ_p[[q−1]] underlying PR.0's acceptance examples. Everything PR.0–PR.8 actually plans — prisms and envelopes, the relative and absolute sites, all of the comparisons, the Nygaard filtration, F-crystals and the logarithmic theory — is missing.

PerfectoidShimuraVarieties.summary: None of this roadmap is in the baseline. There is no Shimura variety, Shimura datum, canonical model, modular curve, Siegel or Hilbert modular variety, no toroidal or minimal compactification, no canonical subgroup, no Hodge–Tate period map, and no diamond or v-sheaf anywhere in Mathlib or Tau Ceti — the 95 Tau Ceti files that mention 'Shimura' cite his book in Hecke-operator docstrings, the files matching 'Hodge–Tate' are about the classical Tate Hodge structure ℤ(m), and the 'diamond' hits are typeclass diamonds and Hecke diamond operators. The classical material that a formalisation would start from is present and substantial: Mathlib's congruence subgroups Γ(N), Γ₀(N), Γ₁(N), the upper half plane with its action, modular forms with q-expansions, elliptic curves, the adele ring of a number field and the finite adele ring of a Dedekind domain, symplectic groups and Grassmannians, plus Tau Ceti's abelian varieties as proper geometrically integral group schemes with isogenies and its very large Hecke-ring and Hecke-slash development (including the adjugate level normalization S5 names). Everything S0–S6 plans — the p-level towers and their limits, perfectoid representability for Siegel, Hodge and pre-abelian data, the period maps, and the modular/Hilbert comparisons — is missing, and so are the prerequisites it imports from PerfectoidSpaces P7/P8 and PerfectoidQuotients Q4.

Mathlib has the classical congruence subgroups Γ(N), Γ₀(N), Γ₁(N) of SL(2,ℤ) and cofiltered categories, but no Shimura datum, no canonical model and no level tower.
